correctness.rationale: The claim is correct for rho,g>0, 0<k1<k2, h,D>0, massless unstressed homogeneous elastic plate. From U=(1+b)tanh(t), fixed U gives b=U*coth(t)-1 with exact domain (0,arctanh U) if U<1 and (0,infinity) if U>=1. The reduced V map G_U(t)=(1+q^4 b(t))*tanh(qt) has the exact derivative 2q^4*tanh(qt)*[(1+q^4*b)/(q^3*sinh(2*q*t))-(1+b)/sinh(2*t)]<0 using sinh(2qt)>q*sinh(2t) and 1+q^4*b<q^4*(1+b), for every q>1 and b>0. As t down to zero G->q^5 U; at the other end G->tanh(q*atanh U) for U<1 or 1+q^4*(U-1) for U>=1; endpoints excluded. IVT and strict decrease give necessity, sufficiency and unique recovered (h,D). The forward Jacobian is positive via -tanh(t)*G′(t). All quantifiers and strict boundaries including U=1 have been checked. An independent high-precision test of 120 sample triples corroborated the algebra and numerical reconstruction; it is not used as an infinite proof.
residual_risks: No formal Lean proof or independent laboratory validation; the analytic argument is the evidence for unlimited parameters.
At q close to 1, very deep water or a near-zero rigidity limit the inversion may be badly conditioned; strict uniqueness is not a quantitative noise-stability bound.
Massless, unstressed and lossless homogeneous sheet, known g and rho, and measured k values are necessary model assumptions; no thickness/Young modulus separation.

evidence: Marchenko, Morozov and Muzylev (2013), measurements section: three pressure gauges at a common frequency infer k and H from pressure ratios, then flexural stiffness using known dispersion; their observation map differs.
Clamond and Labarbe (2023), arXiv:2310.20311, section 4: spatial bottom-pressure profiles recover free-surface and surface-pressure quantities, not the two-sampled dispersion map.

Sergienko (2017), DOI 10.1002/2017JC012947: simplified ice-shelf group-speed observations estimate Young modulus under an independently constrained geometry; no stated arbitrary positive h,D two-point image.

Voermans et al. (2023), arXiv:2305.06490: field-wave inversion with inertial and constitutive parameters; results on observational identifiability are not a global two-parameter noise-free inverse theorem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A more elaborate hydroelastic model, pressure sensor method, or practical wave inversion does not dominate a theorem about exactly two prescribed wavenumber-frequency pairs without a demonstrated specialization and global injectivity/image conclusion. Inspected sections do not contain an implication supplying the exact interval L_q(U)<V<q^5 U for every q>1. Existing inverse methodology is acknowledged, not rebranded as new.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality is accepted for the exact noise-free global bijection and sharp two-frequency realizability interval, not for the classical flexural-gravity forward dispersion law. Direct comparisons with accessible original manuscripts show that previously established forward laws, pressure-sensor inversions, field-wave inversions, and bottom-pressure reconstructions use different observables or do not establish this necessary-and-sufficient two-mode data image. The scalar derivative calculation is elementary once formulated, so unlocated specialized inverse literature remains a priority risk; negative search results do not certify novelty.
residual_risks: Unlocated specialized inverse flexural-gravity literature may already imply the global two-frequency region despite different terminology; negative search is not novelty certification.

The inverse follows from the known forward law by a short but nontrivial monotonic elimination; depending on editorial standards it may be regarded as an elementary corollary rather than a large conceptual advance.

value.rationale: Depth h and plate rigidity D are distinct natural unknown physical coefficients in an established flexural-gravity dispersion relation; two independent wavenumber-frequency observations are the minimal nontrivial joint identification design. Beyond the known forward formula, the theorem provides the entire attainable measurement region for every q>1, a sharp if-and-only-if feasibility test, a globally unique scalar reconstruction and the correct weak-conditioning caveats. This exact invariant of the two-observation inverse map can be used to rule out inconsistent ideal-model data or ambiguity without arbitrary fitting. The result is modest in scope (elementary hyperbolic inequalities, no noisy inverse theory) but a meaningful complete natural classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
residual_risks: No uncertainty quantification for finite-precision data; model misspecification may overwhelm exact-feasibility test.
Value is the precise idealized two-parameter inverse classification rather than a new dispersion law or broad wave inverse method.

limitations: Physical model assumes linear inviscid fluid, known density/gravity, massless unstressed homogeneous plate, known distinct wavenumbers and exact frequencies.
The two recovered parameters are depth and composite bending rigidity, not independent elastic modulus and ice thickness.
The theorem is not a stable noisy inverse guarantee, and the numerical checks are not an infinite proof.
Originality is best-of-knowledge and acknowledges published forward law, different inverse methods and specialized-literature residual risk.
Confidentiality-safe public metadata replacements were not staged; a scientific PASS is not permission to publish unchanged operational provenance or misleading first-publication dates.
